title: A spilling formula whose size neither its text nor what it reads gives shows one value in Google Sheets
symptom: a dynamic array formula written to spill without its range (Python `spill=True`, Rust `Spill::Anchor`, CLI `set --formula --spill`, edit map `"spill": true`) is written over its result's range when the formula tells how large the result is, exactly (`SORT(A2:A10)`, `A2:A10*2`, `SEQUENCE(5)`) or at most (`UNIQUE(A2:A10)`, `FILTER(A2:C10,C2:C10>0)`: the range they read). When nothing in the formula gives that size (a size read from a cell, as in `SEQUENCE(B1)` or `EXPAND(A1:B2,B1)`; `GROUPBY`, `PIVOTBY`, `TEXTSPLIT`; a function whose extent is not read yet, such as `XLOOKUP`, `INDEX`, `OFFSET`, `MAP` or `BYROW`; a table reference such as `Sales[Amount]`; a LAMBDA; a result the data size over whole columns or rows, as `UNIQUE(A:A)` or `FILTER(A:C,C:C>0)`; a result the data size whose largest range meets a value, another array formula or a merge, or covers more than a million cells), it is stored on its cell alone (`<f t="array" ref="J2">`, as XlsxWriter stores it): Excel spills it when it opens the workbook, but Google Sheets takes the extent from `ref` and shows the first value alone. Only an evaluator knows that size: the evaluator of the second set (#724) writes the extent of every spilling formula
workaround: give the range the result fills, from the formula's cell, its other cells empty (a wider range is fine: Excel and Google Sheets leave the rest empty): `spill="J2:J5"` in Python, `Spill::Range` in Rust, `--spill-range J2:J5` or `"spill": "J2:J5"` in the CLI
